# Spinner

Indeterminate loading: three quarters of a circle, turning. Use it when a wait has no measurable progress — `Progress` is the one that knows how far along it is.

- **Import:** `import { Spinner } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Feedback
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/feedback-spinner--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { Spinner, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function SpinnerExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <Spinner />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Spinner

Indeterminate loading: the system's arc, turning, with a name to hear.

The sizes are the `Spinner/size/*` tokens — 16, 24, 32 and 48 — and iOS,
Android and Figma draw the same four. The turn is the system's own
`kozmos-spin`, one second, linear, and it stops under
`prefers-reduced-motion` (GAP-50); the status role keeps saying so when it
does, which is why the label is not decorative.

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `SpinnerProps`, which extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.

- `size`: `"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"`, optional, default `"md"`.

  Written out rather than named, because `scripts/skills/check-variant-parity
.mjs` reads the union from the interface: behind a type alias the axis is
  invisible to it, and Spinner dropped out of the parity scan entirely the
  first time this was written the other way round.

- `label`: `string`, optional, default `"Loading"`.

  What assistive technology hears while the wait lasts.

- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Also exported

- `SpinnerSize` (type).

  ```ts
  type SpinnerSize = NonNullable<SpinnerProps["size"]>;
  ```
